Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires are on the field. Dasun Shanaka is giving some last-minute instructions to his team as they are seen in a huddle along the boundary rope. Imam-ul-Haq and Abdullah Shafique stride out to open the batting innings for Pakistan as they begin the journey to the target. Sri Lanka introduces spin early on in the innings as Maheesh Theekshana will have the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, that was an amazing first innings and we saw both teams dominating each other during different phases of the game. The Lankans have managed to put 344 on the board courtesy of centuries from Kusal Mendis and Sadeera Samarawickrama. Hasan Ali's 4-wicket haul helped Pakistan to put the pressure on the batters. Will Pakistan manage to chase down its mammoth total or will the Lankan bowlers prevail? We will find out soon. Grab a cup of coffee and join us back for the chase.

One of the two centurions for Sri Lanka, Sadeera Samarawickrama is in for a chat. He says that he is really happy since it was his maiden ODI hundred. Credits Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis for the way they batted. Shares that his plan was to bat positively and give the strike to Mendis. Adds that it was a great partnership between them. Mentions that the wicket was good in the first few overs. Adds that the ball started gripping in the last few overs. Feels that once the ball gets old, taking the pace off will be a good option.

Pakistan had a very strong start to the innings by taking Kusal Perera's wicket off Hasan Ali's bowling. However, the bowlers couldn't maintain the pressure after that and allowed a few partnerships to be made by the Lankan batters. Shadab Khan stepped up and took a very crucial wicket of Pathum Nissanka. The bowlers were again dominated by the Lankans in the middle phases. Hasan Ali was the main attraction as he clinched the wickets of both centurions and gave crucial breakthroughs. After the dismissal of Dhananjaya de Silva, it was all about the bowling. Hasan Ali came to the rescue with a crucial 4-wicket haul along with Haris Rauf providing a strong end with his 2 wickets. A strong display at the end of the innings helped restrict the Lankans to 344 runs.

It's a very good score put on the board by Sri Lanka, it might be just enough to give a challenge to Pakistan to chase it down. At the start of the innings, Kusal Perera couldn't hold up to Hasan Ali's bowling, but after that, Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis put pressure back on the bowlers which favored Sri Lanka and allowed the batters to be aggressive. Pathum Nissanka was sent back to the pavilion just as he was setting the tone of the game, but Kusal Mendis carried on and played an exceptional innings. Sadeera Samarawickrama supported him throughout the innings and kept the scoreboard going. Both, Kusal Mendis and Sadeera Samarawickrama reached their centuries and made sure that their team reached a total of 344.

What an entertaining first innings it was, thanks to the amazing batting display by the Lankan batters who took apart the bowlers. This game saw two centurions the first one being Kusal Mendis followed by a maiden ODI ton by Sadeera Samarawickrama. A special knock by both of them along with a fifty by Pathum Nissanka helped Sri Lanka reach a very respectable total of 344.

Haris Rauf has his second wicket and Sri Lanka end up with 344 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the pre-game formalities. Sunny skies greet the two umpires as they make their way out to the middle. Babar Azam with some final instructions in the Pakistan huddle near the ropes before they disperse. They are followed by the two Sri Lankan openers, Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Perera. Shaheen Afridi will start with the new ball for Pakistan. Two slips in place. Off we go...

We are moments away from the start of this clash, but before that, the match officials and the two sets of players will line up for the national anthems. It will be Sri Lanka's national anthem first followed by the national anthem of Pakistan.

Pakistan's skipper Babar Azam says that the pitch looks dry and feels that the first ten overs will be crucial with the ball. Mentions that they have played a few games in Hyderabad and are used to the conditions here. Adds that they will look to utilise the conditions. Feels that the opening has not been up to the mark and informs that they have made one change with Abdullah Shafique coming in for Fakhar Zaman. On their record against Sri Lanka in ODI World Cups, he says that such record gives you confidence and they have taken confidence from the previous game as well.

The skipper of Sri Lanka, Dasun Shanaka says that they will bat first. Feels that the pitch will assist the spinner in the later part of the game. He adds that scoring runs in the last game was very pleasing and mentions that Maheesh Theekshana comes in for Kasun Rajitha. He also says that he hopes that they will tick the right boxes in this game and will work on getting all variations right.
